reason: The cave needs light, and fire is the obvious available source.
expectation: Fire will light the cave interior for painting.

effect: The cave is lit, and painting an animal from memory is now a goal.
reaction: The fire provided the expected practical first step.
reason: Weathered rock can contain pigment, and water may make it usable as paint.
expectation: The rock and water will make a painting material.

effect: The pigment is ready for painting on the lit cave wall.
reaction: The rock and water made the expected paint.
reason: The lit cave provides the surface for the pigment, and the goal calls for an animal from memory.
expectation: The community will use the pigment in the cave to paint an animal from memory.

effect: The pigment and memory produced an animal painting; the next goal is to add stars.
reaction: The automatic use of memory made the painting step straightforward.
reason: Stars are available, and the new goal asks for them in the painting.
expectation: Stars will be added to the cave painting.

effect: The animal painting now includes stars, completing that goal; making a song and passing on knowledge remain.
reaction: The added stars brought the two subjects together as expected.
reason: A call provides sound, and a story could give a song something to express; this is a guess.
expectation: The call and story may form a song.

effect: The call produced an echo in the painted cave rather than combining with the story; the echo may help make a song.
reaction: The automatic echo was an unexpected but understandable result.
reason: An echo repeats sound, so pairing it with the story is a plausible next attempt toward a song, though I am guessing.
expectation: The echo and story may inspire a song.

alternatives.reason: I could check its available partners before guessing.

effect: Echo combined automatically with memory to make a song; passing on what the community learned remains.
reaction: The remembered rhythm explains the song, though my story guess was wrong.
reason: A song can be taught, and the shared discovery is knowledge the community can pass on; this is a guess.
expectation: The community may use the song to pass on its discovery.

alternatives.reason: Checking its partners could clarify how it contributes to teaching.

effect: Song has no available combination, so I need another route to passing on knowledge.
reaction: The failed guess leaves the teaching step unclear.
reason: Shared discovery is the knowledge to pass on, so checking its available partners should reveal how to teach it.
expectation: The inspection will show what can help communicate the discovery.

effect: Inspecting Shared discovery revealed Story as its sole partner and automatically produced Teaching, completing the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying that teaching included both explaining evidence and practising skills.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making Teaching was most worthwhile: it connected the earlier discovery to explaining a prediction, checking it and practising skills.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying Song with Shared discovery was least worthwhile; the failed guess did not advance the teaching goal.

surprise.text: I expected a story to help make the song, but the cave produced an echo and memory turned its sounds into a rhythm instead.

arbitrary.text: Adding stars directly to the painted cave felt somewhat symbolic rather than a practical painting step, though the goal made its purpose clear.

continue.text: Yes. I would try another chapter for the combination of making and concise explanations, especially when the results connect an action to how an idea works.
